display.title: Ahavas Yisroel: Rabbi Akiva's Great Rule of the Torah
display.summary_short: Rabbi Akiva calls 'love your fellow as yourself' a great rule of the Torah; Uncle Yossi explains why loving every Jew leads to loving Hashem.
display.summary_long: A short teaching from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, recorded during the Three Weeks. Uncle Yossi recalls Rabbi Akiva's famous saying from the Gemara: the mitzvah to love your fellow as yourself is not just another rule, but a great rule of the Torah. When we truly love one another, we can truly love Hashem and keep all the other mitzvos. As the Alter Rebbe taught, Ahavas Yisroel leads to Ahavas Hashem. He gives a simple example: to show real love for a friend, you show that you also love the friends he loves. Hashem says He loves every one of us, so to show our love for Hashem we must love those He loves. This matters especially in the Three Weeks, since the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed because we lacked Ahavas Yisroel.
display.lesson: Loving every Jew is the way to show our love for Hashem.

date.note: 'Especially today, during the Three Weeks'; cut from episode 184. The same talk aired in episode 135 (Three Weeks 5744).

sources_cited.note: Rabbi Akiva: 'Love your fellow as yourself' (Vayikra 19:18) is a great rule of the Torah.

quality.notes: Opens by referring to Rabbi Akiva from the preceding story in the broadcast, but stands on its own.
